scene_translation: The woman slipped into a small coffee shop at the end of the alley. You followed, pushing open the door — the smell of tobacco and coffee hit you at once. Inside it was dim; an elderly proprietor slowly polished cups behind the counter. The woman in the blue raincoat had already taken a seat by the window. She looked at you and said quietly, "You finally came, Tesuto. I need to talk to you about this notebook."
grammar_note: 【やっと〜てくれた】'やっと' means 'finally/at last', expressing that something took longer than expected. Combined with 〜てくれた (someone did something for the speaker's benefit), it carries a tone of relief — 'you finally came (for me).' Notice the woman speaks in casual register (くれたね, 話さないといけないから) — this suggests familiarity she has no right to have with a stranger.

mystery_memo: The woman in the blue raincoat has led the player to a dim retro kissaten in the alley behind Tokyo Station — her chosen ground, suggesting she planned this encounter. She knows the player's name and has explicitly referenced the notebook, confirming she placed it deliberately. The old proprietor is a new figure to watch; his calm presence may be more than incidental. The woman's casual speech register implies false intimacy — she speaks as though they share history. Player relationship with woman: cautious/neutral. Notebook remains the central object; its contents are still unknown.
